Part 2. What gets in the way

The program works and its tests pass. The weaknesses below aren't bugs; they're the reasons each new feature costs more than the last. They are grouped by cause.

2.1 The shape exists only while it is being painted

Because stitches are computed and painted in one step, anything else that needs the shape has to get it some other way:

  • discs through infrastructure();
  • bounds collected as a side effect while drawing;
  • thumbnails by borrowing the main canvas;
  • a printed template would have to be drawn all over again.
Every one of these is a second account of the same geometry.

2.2 One thing, many owners

A registry object is a single shared copy, so Draw, Figures and Patterns end up sharing one set of settings. Inside an object, end points are kept twice: once by name and once in points[]. Across a figure, a welded spot is kept once per layer. Wherever there are copies, code has to keep them in step, and that's where the bugs have been, including both Phase 8 bugs found in real use.

[[FIG copies_vs_one | Copies kept in step, against one entry with two names]]

2.3 Every change is final

There is no undo. Delete Layer warns that it can't be taken back. In a program meant for sketching, where trying something and backing out is the point, that's a real cost.

2.4 Adding something takes bookkeeping

A new script shows up only after a restart or a Rebuild, because its folder's manifest has to be rewritten. A new Draw object needs a line added by hand to drawRegistry.js. boxes.js shows what happens when that step is missed: it's loaded and never appears, and nothing says why. The manifests are copies of what's in the folders, so they can disagree with the folders. That's why there are start-up rebuilds, missing-file checks and an alert bar.

2.5 Scripts share one room

Every script draws on the same canvas with the same shared state. One script can leave something behind that the next one trips on. Two scripts fail after about a hundred others have run.

2.6 Two kinds of drawing, two kinds of code

Parametric drawings live in their own code (drawParametrics.js). The good tools for spacing points (even spacing by arc length, bias, jitter, all in createNodes) work only for ellipses. A rose curve can't use them.

2.7 Small things that add up

Controls are declared in two blocks, with widget names instead of value types, and with two names for the colour widget. "Overlay" means three different things. Each tab builds its menus its own way. None of these is serious alone; together they make every change start with "which convention does this part use?"
